quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see the roadway through vehicles in front of you.
When the weather is pleasant and clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make stopping harder. This includes heavy traffic, slippery roads, poor weather, nighttime, and when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands over the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands over the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes. This is especially important when riding through areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which is NOT important?
questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards, fits snugly all around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for protection.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered legally intoxicated for someone age 21 or older?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: If a driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down. A tailgater may be focused on you and not see upcoming hazards that require everyone to slow down.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you on your left, where should you ride?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help the driver.
Move to the shoulder to help the driver.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either edge increases the risk of a collision because the passing driver may merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the roadway, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as possible before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact to lighten the front end.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes with road and traffic conditions. Adjust your position to stay safe and make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What is true about rounded, convex motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They are easy to get used to right away.
They make cars seem closer than they really are.
They provide a narrow view of the road.
They make cars seem farther away than they really are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars seem farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors but make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to them.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. They tell riders the rules of the road. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, group riders should:

options.text: Ride on the far right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single line
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern is usually best. But when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway, switch to a single line.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's total stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you
Does not mean they see you

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver sees you just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle but still fail to notice it.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Almost never need to be replaced
Will get scratches and become brittle, so replace them regularly
Should be made of breakable material so they break away in a crash
Should not allow air to pass through

questions.correctAnswerText: Will get scratches and become brittle, so replace them regularly
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are plastic and will scratch and become brittle over time. Replace them often to keep them working well and to stay comfortable.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Slow down first, then speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down first, then speed up
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, shift to a lower gear and slow down as you approach it. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
Near the back of the group
At the very end of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay just behind the leader. This keeps them from chasing the group and allows more experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handlebar grip toward the direction you want to go
Press the handlebar grip away from the direction you want to go

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip toward the direction you want to go
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handlebar grip on the side you want to turn toward. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Switch back and forth between the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, even for regular stops that are not emergencies.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each lane give a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each lane gives a motorcycle three paths: the left side, the middle, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: What happens if you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: Braking works the same as on a straight road.
You have more traction when leaning into the curve.
You may have less traction when leaning into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction when leaning into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When the motorcycle leans into a turn, some tire traction is used for turning. This means less traction is available for braking.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you farthest away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars is still on the road and hasn't washed away yet. Riding in the tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and let each rider go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned spot later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the rest of the group, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a set location later.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Grab the front brake lever quickly.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
Gradually increase pressure on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front wheel gets more traction. Apply more force to the front brake while using less pressure on the rear brake. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Do not drag your feet on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Don't drag your feet on the road, as they could catch on something and cause you to lose control. Always watch for other traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an approved helmet type?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-quarter
questions.explanation: Approved helmets come in one-half, three-quarter, and full-face styles. A full-face helmet offers the best protection.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Brake and swerve as separate actions. Do one first, then do the other. Do not do both at the same time.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and don't use it again.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake completely and immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen the most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors while riding to help others see you. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group
At the back of the group

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: Which lane position should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No lane position should always be avoided

questions.correctAnswerText: No lane position should always be avoided
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: As your weight moves forward while braking, what happens?

options.text: You can apply the front brake harder
You should reduce front brake pressure
You can apply the rear brake harder

questions.correctAnswerText: You can apply the front brake harder
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, the front wheel has more grip. This means you can apply the front brake with more force.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while slowly increasing front brake pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle creates a wind blast, where should you ride to have the most room for error?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane
In the center portion of the lane
In the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane gives you the most room to react if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: A rider can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When the left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level is considered legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person who is 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: How can you increase visibility at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers
Always ride with your headlight on
Ride close to vehicles in front of you

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position yourself so oncoming drivers can see you clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Eye contact alone is not enough to ensure a driver sees you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, which lane position should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Use the left portion of the lane when passing on the left. This improves your view of oncoming traffic and makes you more visible.

questions.question: When braking on your bike, as weight moves to the front, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Not worry. Weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: As you brake, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever. The weight of the bike moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fit snugly, and have no visible damage. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage others to talk them out of driving.
Find another way for them to get home.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Keep them busy to slow their drinking pace.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from driving drunk, you can find other transportation, involve them in activities to slow their drinking, keep them from leaving until sober, and get friends to help stop them. Do not tell them to use different roads.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it blocks horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always wear hearing protection to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs and hearing protection guard against damage while still allowing you to hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When exiting a highway in a group, which formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding on straight roads. Switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the inexperienced rider to lead.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to stop someone from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking.
Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Effective ways to prevent drunk driving include arranging another ride home, keeping them busy with activities, using any reason to keep them from leaving, and getting friends involved. Waiting 15 minutes does not work.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, adjust the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the recommended settings for the extra weight.

questions.question: Motorcycle windshields:

options.text: Are a good substitute for a face shield.
Are a good substitute for goggles.
Will not protect your eyes from the wind.
Protect against objects thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not an adequate substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.
